title: Unemployment
competency: Distinguish employed, unemployed and not in the labour force, calculate unemployment and participation rates, and explain the types of unemployment.

keywords.def: The number of people employed plus the number unemployed.
Being without a job while looking for one (or on temporary layoff).
Unemployment while workers search and are matched with jobs, e.g. new graduates.
Unemployment caused by too little aggregate demand in a recession or depression.
Lasting unemployment from a mismatch between labour demand and supply: skills, location, technology, economic structure.
Working in a job below one's training or purpose, or working full time but earning too little to escape poverty.

ideas.name: Labour force and the unemployment rate

en.text: A person is employed if they work at a paid job, unemployed if they have no job and are looking for one (or are on temporary layoff), and otherwise not in the labour force, like a full-time student or a retiree. The labour force is employed plus unemployed; the unemployment rate is unemployed ÷ labour force × 100; the participation rate is labour force ÷ adult population × 100. Unemployment wastes output, so keeping it low is a policy priority.

am.text: የሰው ኃይል = ተቀጣሪዎች + ሥራ አጦች። የሥራ አጥነት መጠን = ሥራ አጦች ÷ የሰው ኃይል × 100። ተማሪዎችና ጡረተኞች በሰው ኃይሉ ውስጥ አይቆጠሩም።

screens.title: Is she unemployed?
screens.ask: Hiwot is a full-time student at Addis Ababa University. She is not looking for a job. Is she unemployed?
opts: No: she is not in the labour force
screens.after: Unemployed means no job AND looking for one. Students and retirees who are not looking are outside the labour force.

screens.title: Employed, unemployed, or not in the labour force?
paras: Employed: spends some time working at a paid job.
Unemployed: no job, and looking for one or on temporary layoff.
Not in the labour force: neither, e.g. a full-time student or a retiree.
The book gives Ethiopia's working age as 14 to 60; formal employment needs age 18.
It excludes children under 14, people over 60, and people in mental and correctional institutions.

screens.title: Why unemployment matters
paras: It affects people most directly and severely.
Unemployed workers are unused resources.
Its opportunity cost is the output they could have produced.
So low unemployment is a public policy priority.

screens.title: Measuring it
paras: Labour force = number employed + number unemployed.
Unemployment rate = (number unemployed ÷ labour force) × 100.
Labour-force participation rate = (labour force ÷ adult population) × 100.
The labour force is a number of people, not a percentage.

screens.title: Worked example
steps: Adult population 60 million; employed 40 million; unemployed 5 million.
Trap: 5 ÷ 60 is wrong; divide by the labour force.

It should divide by the employed only

en.text: Frictional unemployment comes from the time it takes to match job seekers with jobs, as for new graduates. Cyclical unemployment comes from too little aggregate demand in a depression, for example when overseas demand for coffee falls. Structural unemployment is a lasting mismatch between labour demand and supply — missing skills, immobility, a labour force growing faster than capital — and education and retraining reduce it. Underemployment means working below one's training or earning too little to escape poverty.

am.text: የሥራ አጥነት ዓይነቶች፡ የሽግግር (ሥራ ፍለጋ)፣ ዑደታዊ (የፍላጎት እጥረት)፣ መዋቅራዊ (የክህሎት አለመመጣጠን)። ከአቅም በታች መቀጠርም አለ።

screens.title: Typists and computers
screens.ask: Offices replace typists with computers. Typists without computer skills cannot find work for years. Why are they jobless?
opts: Their skills no longer match the jobs available
They are between two jobs for a week
The economy is in a short recession
screens.after: A lasting mismatch between skills and jobs is structural unemployment.

screens.title: Three major types
paras: Frictional: workers moving between jobs; matching takes time.
Example: new graduates searching for a first job.
Cyclical: too little aggregate demand in a business depression (Dewett, 1997).
Example: overseas demand for coffee falls; in a recession workers are laid off.
Structural: a lasting mismatch between labour demand and supply.
Causes: missing skills, labour immobility, labour force growing faster than capital, machine breakdowns, raw-material shortages.
Education and retraining reduce structural unemployment.
screens.note: Not knowing where the jobs are is a search problem, so this lesson counts it as frictional.

screens.title: Underemployment
paras: A person takes a job below their training or purpose.
Or works full time but earns too little to rise above poverty.
Open and disguised unemployment: about 30–35 % of the labour force in underdeveloped countries.

items: A worker quits to find a better job nearby

opts: Waiting for the recession to end

screens.why: p.14: workers are laid off when demand falls in a recession.

screens.text: The opportunity cost of unemployment is
opts: the output the unemployed workers could have produced
the wages paid to employed workers
screens.ans: the output the unemployed workers could have produced
screens.clue: What is lost when workers sit idle?

screens.text: A country's labour force grows faster than its stock of capital, so many new workers cannot find productive jobs for years. Which type is this?
opts: None: they are not in the labour force
screens.why: p.14 lists a labour force growing faster than capital as a structural cause: the economy's structure cannot absorb them.
screens.clue: Is it short, demand-driven, or lasting?

notes.text: p.12: the book gives working age as 14–60 and formal employment from 18. Ethiopia's Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019 sets 15 as the minimum employment age, and statistics often use 15–64. The lesson keeps "the book gives …"; please check before teaching as fact.
p.13: "the total labour force refers to the percentage of the population …" — the labour force is a number of people; the percentage is the participation rate.

p.14: lack of knowledge about available jobs or workers is a search/matching problem (frictional), but the book lists it under structural. The lesson keeps frictional = short search, structural = lasting mismatch.
All numeric examples and the employed/unemployed sorting are added; the book has formulas but no worked numbers.
